title: Book 74

beats.what: Reverend opens sermon with chaos-and-faith duality, setting the episode's theological frame
Tabitha asks the Reverend point-blank whether they are dead; he deflects with purgatory logic then confirms they are alive
Jade discovers the town lamp cords contain no wire, exposing the electricity as impossible and unknowable
Reverend reveals to a bound Sara that she may be living inside Book 74, the unwritten continuation of the Bible
Sara convulses and produces a drawing that proves the voices watched Boyd bury his bag on arrival day
Boyd reveals his Parkinson's diagnosis to Kenny and gives him the option to delay the forest expedition
Tabitha discovers her lost bracelet -- made from her father-in-law's boot laces -- sitting impossibly in the basement
A creature approaches the Reverend's doorstep asking when it can come inside, ending the episode

character_beats.beat: Wants to launch a solo forest expedition to find a way home before his illness progresses; defers departure when Kenny needs him present as a father rather than a commander
Positions himself as Sara's protector and theological guide; secretly holds her restrained in the church while engineering a reason to join Boyd's journey
Driven to find rational explanations for the town's anomalies; recruits an antagonistic engineer through apology and shared purpose
Seeks metaphysical certainty about whether they are alive; then pivots to physical investigation -- chasing the basement wires toward a tangible answer

key_lines.line: Would it matter? We'd still be stuck.
key_lines.why: Reverend's pragmatic non-answer to the alive/dead question; reframes the entire season's existential urgency
Names the episode and seeds the theological spine: the town as a living scripture not yet written

key_lines.line: They said they watched you bury the bag
key_lines.why: First verifiable proof the voices have independent knowledge, raising Sara from unreliable to crucial
Boyd's disclosure recontextualises every prior urgency beat; his clock is medical, not just situational
Private proof the bracelet is authentic; marks the impossible intrusion of the Matthews' past into this place

open_loops: What entity is communicating through Sara, and what is its actual agenda toward the townspeople?
Where do the basement wires go, and what is powering the town's electricity?
Why does Boyd's buried bag contain blood along with his shirt?
How did the bracelet -- lost at a hospital years before arrival -- end up in the town basement?
Who or what is knocking on the Reverend's door asking to come inside?

contradiction.wants: To leave immediately for the forest while he still has the physical capacity to find a way home
contradiction.does: Stays in town and plays catch with Kenny after Kristi's appeal that Kenny needs a father, not a sheriff

tone_notes: The episode opens at its highest dialogue density (157 words/min in minute 1, the recap) then drops into a slow theological gear. Minutes 7-10 are essentially silent (density 4, 0, 0) -- the longest stretch of quiet in the run, spanning 128 seconds from 07:52 to 10:00 -- which isolates Tabitha's church visit as a set piece outside the town's noise. A second near-silence at minutes 6-7 (density 55, 4) brackets the walk to the church. Density spikes to 166 at minute 12 during the wire-discovery scene, then collapses through minutes 16-17 (density 38) as Jade falls from the tree. The back third of the episode pulses in and out of silence around the Boyd-Kenny baseball exchange (two separate 78-80 second silences in minutes 44-47), giving the farewell its weight.
